drivingQuestion: Does a minor have halakhically effective thought, and if so in what respect and by what authority — Torah law or rabbinic law?
outcomeNote: In the second version R' Yoḥanan himself resolves the dilemma (ופשיט), and Rav Huna supplies both verses Shmuel asked for.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, בָּעֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: קָטָן יֵשׁ לוֹ מַחְשָׁבָה, אוֹ אֵין לוֹ מַחְשָׁבָה?
segments.en: § «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan raises a dilemma:» In matters that require thought and intent, «does a minor have» halakhically effective «thought, or does he not have» halakhically effective «thought?»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי: וְתִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה? מַאי שְׁנָא מַעֲשֶׂה דְּלָא קָא מִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ – דִּתְנַן: ״יֵשׁ לָהֶן מַעֲשֶׂה״? מַחְשָׁבָה נָמֵי לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ, דִּתְנַן: ״אֵין לָהֶן מַחְשָׁבָה״!
segments.en: «Rabbi Ami said to» Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba: «And let» Rabbi Yoḥanan «raise this dilemma» with regard to the «action» of a minor, whether the action of a minor that indicates intent is effective. «What is different» about the «action» of a minor «that» Rabbi Yoḥanan «does not raise a dilemma?» Is it due to the fact «that we learned» in a mishna (Kelim 17:15): A deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor «have» the capacity to perform «an action» that is halakhically effective? With regard to «thought as well let him not raise this dilemma, as we learned» in the same mishna: «They do not have» the capacity for halakhically effective «thought.»

segments.he: דִּתְנַן: הָאַלּוֹן, וְהָרִמּוֹן, וְהָאֱגוֹז שֶׁחֲקָקוּם תִּינוֹקוֹת לָמוֹד בָּהֶן עָפָר, אוֹ שֶׁהִתְקִינוּם לְכַף מֹאזְנַיִם – טְמֵאִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן מַעֲשֶׂה,
segments.en: «As we learned» in that mishna: With regard to «an acorn, a pomegranate, or a nut, which minors hollowed» in order «to measure dirt with them or that they affixed to a scale,» the halakhic status of those shells is that of vessels, and they are «susceptible to ritual impurity.» By contrast, if the minors merely thought to use the shells for measuring or weighing, unlike adults, they do not thereby render those shells into vessels. The reason for this distinction is «due to» the fact «that they have» the capacity to perform «an action,»
«but they do not have» the capacity to effect a halakhic status by means of «thought.»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַחְשָׁבָה גְּרֵידְתָּא לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ, כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ – מַחְשַׁבְתּוֹ נִיכֶּרֶת מִתּוֹךְ מַעֲשָׂיו.
segments.en: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba «said to» Rabbi Ami: With regard to a case of effecting a halakhic status by means of «thought alone,» Rabbi Yoḥanan «does not raise a dilemma. When he raises a dilemma,» it is with regard to a case where «his thought is discernible from his actions.»

segments.he: כְּגוֹן דַּהֲוָה קָיְימָא עוֹלָה בַּדָּרוֹם, וְאַתְיַיהּ בַּצָּפוֹן וְשַׁחְטַהּ, מַאי? מִדְּאַתְיַיהּ בַּצָּפוֹן וְשַׁחְטַהּ אִיכַּוֵּין לַהּ, אוֹ דִילְמָא מָקוֹם הוּא דְּלָא אִיתְרְמִי לֵיהּ?
segments.en: «For example,» in a case «where» an animal that is brought as «a burnt offering was standing in the south» of the Temple courtyard «and» a minor «took it to the north» of the courtyard, the designated place for its slaughter, «and slaughtered it» there, «what» is the halakha? Can one conclude «from» the fact «that he took it to the north and slaughtered» it there that «he had» the «intent to» slaughter the animal for the sake of a burnt offering; «or perhaps» he moved the animal to the north because «a place did not happen» to be available «for him» in the south?

segments.he: הָא נָמֵי אַמְרַהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲדָא זִימְנָא, דִּתְנַן: הַמַּעֲלֶה פֵּירוֹתָיו לַגַּג מִפְּנֵי הַכְּנִימָה, וְיָרַד עֲלֵיהֶם טַל – אֵינָן בְּ״כִי יוּתַּן״, וְאִם נִתְכַּוֵּין לְכָךְ – הֲרֵי הֵן בְּ״כִי יוּתַּן״.
segments.en: Rabbi Ami asked: But with regard to «this» matter, «too, Rabbi Yoḥanan» already «said» a conclusive resolution «one time, as we learned» in a mishna (Makhshirin 6:1): In the case of «one who takes his produce up to the roof» to protect it «from insects, and dew fell upon it,» the produce «is not in» the category of the verse: “But «when» water «is placed» upon the seed” (Leviticus 11:38), from which it is derived that produce becomes susceptible to ritual impurity only if it is dampened by one of seven liquids and its owner was agreeable to its dampening. «And if» after taking the produce up to the roof «he intended» that the produce would be dampened by dew, the produce «is in» the category of the verse “But «when» water «is placed» upon the seed.”

segments.he: הֶעֱלוּם חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְכַּוְּונוּ לְכָךְ, אֵינָן בְּ״כִי יוּתַּן״, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן מַעֲשֶׂה וְאֵין לָהֶן מַחְשָׁבָה.
segments.en: That mishna continues: In a case where «a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor took» the produce «up» to the roof, «even if they intended» that the produce would be dampened by dew, the produce «is not in» the category of the verse “But «when» water «is placed» upon the seed” «due to» the fact «that they have» the capacity to perform «an action but they do not have» the capacity for halakhically effective «thought.»

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הִיפֵּךְ בָּהֶן, אֲבָל הִיפֵּךְ בָּהֶן – הֲרֵי זֶה בְּ״כִי יוּתַּן״.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» The tanna «taught» this halakha «only» in a case «where» the minor «did not turn them over. But» if «he turned them over,» indicating that he wants them to be dampened by the dew, the produce «is in» the category of the verse “But «when» water «is placed» upon the seed.” Evidently, Rabbi Yoḥanan rules that when the intention of a minor is apparent from his actions, it is halakhically effective.

segments.he: הָכִי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ: דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא אוֹ דְּרַבָּנַן?
segments.en: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said to Rabbi Ami that «this» is «the dilemma» that Rabbi Yoḥanan «raises:» In a case where the intent of a minor is clear from his actions, is the fact that his thought is effective «by Torah law or by rabbinic law?» That is one version of the exchange between Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Ami.

segments.he: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, בָּעֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: קָטָן יֵשׁ לוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה אוֹ אֵין לוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה?
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak teaches» their exchange in «this» manner. «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan raises a dilemma:» With regard to «a minor, does he have» the capacity to perform «an action» that is halakhically effective «or does he not have» the capacity to perform such «an action?»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי: וְתִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ מַחְשָׁבָה! מַאי שְׁנָא מַחְשָׁבָה דְּלָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ? דִּתְנַן: אֵין לָהֶן מַחְשָׁבָה. מַעֲשֶׂה נָמֵי לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ, דִּתְנַן: יֵשׁ לָהֶן מַעֲשֶׂה.
segments.en: «Rabbi Ami said to» Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba: «And let» Rabbi Yoḥanan «raise this dilemma» with regard to the «thought» of a minor. «What is different» about the «thought» of a minor «that» Rabbi Yoḥanan «does not raise a dilemma?» Is it due to the fact «that we learned» in a mishna (Kelim 17:15): A deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor «do not have» the capacity for effective «thought?» With regard to «action as well let him not raise this dilemma, as we learned» in the same mishna: «They have» the capacity to perform «an action.»

segments.he: הָכִי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ: דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא אוֹ דְּרַבָּנַן? וּפָשֵׁיט: יֵשׁ לָהֶן מַעֲשֶׂה, וַאֲפִילּוּ מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, אֵין לָהֶן מַחְשָׁבָה, וַאֲפִילּוּ מִדְּרַבָּנַן. מַחְשַׁבְתּוֹ נִיכֶּרֶת מִתּוֹךְ מַעֲשָׂיו – מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא אֵין לוֹ, מִדְּרַבָּנַן יֵשׁ לוֹ.
segments.en: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said to Rabbi Ami that «this» is «the dilemma» that Rabbi Yoḥanan «raises:» Is the fact that their actions are effective and their thought is ineffective «by Torah law,» and a minor’s action would consequently be effective even with regard to the sacrifice of a burnt offering, «or» is this fact «by rabbinic law» and it is merely a stringency? «And» Rabbi Yoḥanan «resolves» the dilemma: «They have» the capacity to perform «an action and» it is effective, «even by Torah law.» But «they do not have» the capacity for effective «thought, even by rabbinic law.» Nevertheless, in a case where «his thought is apparent from his actions, by Torah law he does not have» effective thought, and «by rabbinic law he has» effective thought.

segments.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל מֵרַב הוּנָא: מִנַּיִן לַמִּתְעַסֵּק בְּקָדָשִׁים שֶׁהוּא פָּסוּל? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְשָׁחַט אֶת בֶּן הַבָּקָר״, שֶׁתְּהֵא שְׁחִיטָה לְשֵׁם בֶּן בָּקָר. אָמַר לוֹ: זוֹ בְּיָדֵינוּ הִיא, לְעַכֵּב מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לִרְצוֹנְכֶם תִּזְבָּחֻהוּ״, לְדַעְתְּכֶם זְבוּחוּ.
segments.en: § «Shmuel asked Rav Huna: From where» is it derived with regard «to one who acts unawares in» the slaughter of «sacrificial» animals, i.e., he slaughtered without intending to perform the act of slaughter at all, «that» the offering «is disqualified?» Rav Huna said to him that it is derived from a verse, «as it is stated: “And he shall slaughter the young bull”» (Leviticus 1:5), indicating «that the slaughter must be for the sake of a young bull,» i.e., knowing that he is performing an act of slaughter. Shmuel «said to» him: «we» received «this» as an established halakha already «that» one must have intent to slaughter the animal ab initio. But «from where» is it derived that intent to slaughter is «indispensable» even after the fact? It is derived from a verse, as «the verse states: “You shall slaughter it to your will”» (Leviticus 19:5), indicating: «Slaughter» the animal «with your intent,» i.e., in the form of a purposeful action.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי חייא בר אבא, בעי רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: R' Ḥiyya bar Abba reports R' Yoḥanan's dilemma whether a minor has effective thought
moves.about: R' Yoḥanan's dilemma whether a minor has halakhically effective thought

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבי אמי: ותיבעי ליה מעשה
moves.summary: R' Ami objects that the mishna settles thought no less than action, so either both are dilemmas or neither
moves.about: why R' Yoḥanan raised the dilemma about thought and not about action, when one mishna settles both alike

moves.cueHe: דתנן: האלון, והרמון, והאגוז שחקקום תינוקות
moves.summary: the Kelim mishna is quoted in full: hollowed shells are susceptible to impurity because minors have effective action
moves.about: the full wording of the Kelim mishna about the acorn, pomegranate and nut hollowed out by minors

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: מחשבה גרידתא לא קא מיבעיא ליה
moves.summary: the dilemma is not about bare thought but about thought discernible from action
moves.about: that R' Yoḥanan did not ask about thought alone, which the mishna settles

moves.summary: the case is spelled out: a minor moves a burnt offering to the north and slaughters it there
moves.about: narrowing R' Yoḥanan's dilemma to the case where the minor's thought is discernible from his actions

moves.cueHe: הא נמי אמרה רבי יוחנן חדא זימנא
moves.summary: R' Ami objects that R' Yoḥanan already settled discernible intent once before
moves.about: that the dilemma is superfluous because R' Yoḥanan already ruled on discernible intent in the mishna of produce taken up to the roof

moves.summary: the Makhshirin mishna about produce taken to the roof is brought as the evidence
moves.about: the mishna about produce taken up to the roof and dampened by dew

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי יוחנן: לא שנו אלא שלא היפך בהן
moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan limits that mishna to a minor who did not turn the produce over
moves.about: limiting the mishna's denial of effective thought to a minor who did not turn the produce over

moves.cueHe: הכי קא מיבעיא ליה: דאורייתא או דרבנן?
moves.summary: the dilemma was really whether discernible intent works by Torah law or only by rabbinic law
moves.about: that the dilemma is whether effective discernible intent is by Torah law or by rabbinic law

moves.cueHe: רב נחמן בר יצחק מתני הכי
moves.summary: a second version of the whole exchange, with the dilemma set on action rather than thought
moves.about: a second version of the exchange, in which the dilemma is about action rather than thought

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבי אמי: ותיבעי ליה מחשבה
moves.summary: the same objection in mirror image: let him raise the dilemma about thought instead
moves.about: why the dilemma is about action and not thought, when the same mishna settles both

moves.cueHe: הכי קא מיבעיא ליה: דאורייתא או דרבנן?
moves.summary: again, the dilemma is Torah law versus rabbinic law
moves.about: that the dilemma is whether the mishna's rule holds by Torah law or by rabbinic law

moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan resolves: action by Torah law, thought not even rabbinically, discernible intent rabbinically only
moves.about: resolving his own dilemma: action is effective even by Torah law, thought not even by rabbinic law, and discernible intent is effective by rabbinic law only

moves.cueHe: בעא מיניה שמואל מרב הונא: מנין למתעסק בקדשים
moves.summary: Shmuel asks Rav Huna for the source that unawares slaughter of consecrated animals is disqualified
moves.about: from where it is derived that one who acts unawares in slaughtering a sacrificial animal disqualifies it

moves.summary: Rav Huna derives it from and he shall slaughter the young bull
moves.about: supplying the verse that requires purposeful slaughter of a sacrificial animal

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: זו בידינו היא, לעכב מנין?
moves.summary: Shmuel presses: that only shows the requirement ab initio; what makes it indispensable?
moves.about: from where it is derived that the intent is indispensable after the fact and not merely required ab initio

moves.summary: the second verse, to your will, makes purposeful slaughter indispensable
moves.about: supplying the second verse that makes purposeful slaughter indispensable even after the fact

edges.cueHe: תלמוד לומר: לרצונכם תזבחוהו
edges.about: supplying the second verse that makes purposeful slaughter indispensable even after the fact

extras.about: R' Yoḥanan's dilemma, in Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak's version, whether a minor has effective action
the same Kelim mishna, cited now in the reverse order
